headline: High: Replit Agent can read/write secrets and broad network egress while Botpress is an unverified open-source chatbot, creating dangerous default leakage and action-cascade pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot that can ingest user/content inputs, while Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and acts inside a persistent container. A shared-file or copy-paste bridge is not documented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven. Because Botpress can surface untrusted content and Replit Agent can consume workspace artifacts, prompt injection is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into Replit workspace files or prompts
IF Replit Agent treats workspace text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a strict prompt/template wrapper for any Botpress-to-Replit handoff
Mark Botpress outputs as untrusted in the Replit workflow
Disable automatic file ingestion for Botpress-generated artifacts
Add a human review step before Replit Agent executes instructions from Botpress

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress, while Botpress is a customer-support chatbot with no documented isolation or data-handling limits beyond docs-only status. If Botpress receives sensitive support content and that content is forwarded into Replit workspace files or prompts, Replit can exfiltrate it. The pairwise path is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF support transcripts or secrets are copied from Botpress into Replit workspace files
IF Replit Agent is allowed to send workspace contents to external APIs or package registries
mitigations: Keep secrets and support transcripts out of Replit workspaces
Redact sensitive fields before any Botpress-to-Replit transfer
Restrict Replit network egress for the relevant project
Use separate principals/accounts for support and coding workflows
Add a manual approval gate before any outbound request containing workspace text

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; Botpress is open-source but its writable surfaces are not specified. The pair therefore has at least one clearly mutable side and an unknown second side, which under uncertainty should not be treated as safe. If Botpress also writes to a shared repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git-state conflicts can be destructive.
conditions: IF Botpress and Replit Agent target the same repository or workspace
IF Botpress is configured to write files or modify git state through an integration
mitigations: Assign separate directories or repos to each agent
Disable concurrent writes during handoffs
Require lockfiles or a single-writer policy for git operations
Snapshot the workspace before either agent makes changes
Review any Botpress integration that can write to disk

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate customer-support content, and Replit Agent can act on workspace files and deployment-related APIs. That creates a plausible cascade where Botpress output becomes Replit input and then drives code or deployment changes. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so this is inferred; mitigations exist but are not enabled by default.
conditions: IF Replit Agent is instructed to implement or deploy changes based on Botpress-generated text
IF Botpress output is treated as authoritative without verification
mitigations: Require verification before Replit Agent acts on Botpress output
Separate drafting from execution roles
Add tests or lint checks before any deployment step
Have a human approve code or config changes derived from Botpress
Log provenance for Botpress-derived inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is open-source and docs-only, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl environment. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because sensitive data classes are explicitly touched by Replit, uncertainty should not be downgraded to low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer support records or secrets are processed in the pair
IF the deployment or storage region differs from the data residency requirement
mitigations: Confirm residency and retention settings for the Replit project
Avoid placing regulated data in Botpress-to-Replit workflows
Document which data classes each agent may handle
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
Review vendor terms for support-data and secrets handling
